chunks: And will not hear its hissing, and will live for ever in the midst of what their hearts desire.

key_terms.حَسِيسَهَا: its hissing (referring to the sound of Hellfire)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the experience of the blessed in Paradise regarding Hell and their desires?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'hissing' (hasis) of Hell is often interpreted as the subtle, lingering sound of regret or the residual heat of punishment, which the blessed will not hear, signifying their complete detachment from the realm of the wretched. This verse underscores the concept of 'Khulud' (eternity) not just as endless time, but as a state of perfect contentment where the soul's deepest spiritual and physical desires are fulfilled without satiety or change. The absence of Hell's noise highlights the purity of their abode, contrasting the chaotic suffering of the damned with the serene, harmonious existence of the righteous.
